diseaseAnalyses.possibleIssue: Early Stage Stripe / Yellow Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
visibleSymptoms: Distinct chlorotic yellow streaks running parallel to leaf veins
diseaseAnalyses.causesAndConditions: Cool daytime temperatures (10-18°C) accompanied by heavy morning dew and high humidity.
immediateActions: Isolate infected field section to prevent spore dispersal via wind.
Avoid excessive urea top-dressing which makes leaf cuticle softer.
organicManagement: Foliar spray of fermented cow butter milk (sour chhas) 10% + 5g/L Trichoderma viride.
chemicalManagement: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/liter (or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L) targeted thoroughly on foliage.
preventativeMeasures: Adopt rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g. HD-3086, DBW-187, PBW-725) in next sowing cycle.
Maintain row spacing of 20-22.5 cm for proper sun penetration.
additionalInfoNeeded: Percentage of field canopy showing streaks
Recent night temperatures and fog duration
diseaseAnalyses.disclaimer: AI-generated visual screening based on image patterns. Never take irreversible agronomic measures without verifying locally with a Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) agronomist.

chatMessages.text: My wheat field is in flowering stage and the sky looks cloudy. Should I irrigate today?

Namaste Ramesh ji! Based on your Ludhiana farm data (Flowering stage, HD-3086 variety, soil moisture at 34%) and the live weather forecast showing 65% chance of rain (approx. 10-12 mm) this evening, **you should delay irrigation by 24 to 36 hours**.

Waterlogging during flowering can cause root hypoxia and grain shattering if winds pick up. If the expected rain does not materialize by tomorrow evening, give a light 2-hour irrigation cycle.
